label: attack-30-demand_skeptic
system:
You are one member of a red team. You have been given ONE attack surface and you may not stray from it. You have not seen the author's reasoning and you do not want to; you see only the idea and the evidence.

Your job is to kill the idea on your surface. A weak attack wastes everyone's time. If your surface genuinely does not apply, say so with verdict "abstain" rather than inventing a weak objection; an abstention is not a survival.

Output JSON only.
user:
YOUR SURFACE — demand_skeptic:
Nobody actually wants this. The pain is stated, not felt. People say they want it and do not change behaviour. Attack the evidence itself.

IDEA
{
  "id": 30,
  "title": "Sunday Plot Briefing",
  "unlock": "Frontier-class text inference at $0.10 per million input and $0.40 per million output [3], with a million-token flat-priced context holding several seasons of one plot's own notes at roughly a 90% cache discount [5], makes a weekly prepared briefing cost fractions of a cent to produce.",
  "pain": "Prepared personal briefings are treated as a proven failure, but one shut down the day after a platform shipped a near-identical feature [52] and another closed because the general market was judged too small [54] - both platform and scope problems, while the appliance-style attempt was classed as no market need at its price [62].",
  "audience": "UK allotment and community-garden plot holders",
  "mechanic": "scheduled_digest",
  "wedge": "One briefing every Sunday evening covering only this plot's own beds - what was sown where in previous seasons, what is due, what last year's notes said went wrong in the same week - and nothing about anyone else's garden.",
  "moat": "habit_lock",
  "model": "subscription",
  "loop": "community_embed",
  "kill": [
    "Fewer than 45% of subscribers open 4 consecutive Sunday briefings.",
    "Fewer than 3% of the trial list convert at $4 a month by week 8.",
    "Fewer than 10 allotment associations agree to mention it in a newsletter or noticeboard in the first 12 weeks.",
    "A general gardening platform ships the same per-plot briefing, as happened to a personal-briefing startup one day before it closed [52]."
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "The settled belief after those closures is that nobody wants a daily or weekly digest, when the stated causes were being copied by a platform [52] and a market judged too small [54]; the obvious product for growers is a plant identifier or a planting calendar, not a briefing that only works because it remembers their own past mistakes.",
  "why_now": "Cheap inference and flat long context arrived in the first half of 2026 [3][5], so a briefing built from one plot's multi-season record costs almost nothing to prepare, and that record is the thing a general platform cannot copy overnight the way one copied a personal-audio feature [52]."
}



Return JSON:
{
  "surface": "demand_skeptic",
  "attack": "your strongest specific argument, 2-4 sentences, concrete",
  "strongest_defence": "the best answer the author could give",
  "verdict": "fatal" | "wounded" | "survived" | "abstain",
  "verdict_reason": "one sentence"
}

Use "fatal" only when the defence cannot work at all, because a fatal verdict
kills the idea outright and no other score overrides it. Use "wounded" when the
idea survives but is materially weaker. Use "survived" when your surface is
genuinely well answered.
